facts.content: Patient reports anxiety, poor sleep, and palpitations for approximately two months.
facts.source_text: CC: Anxiety, poor sleep, palpitations x ~2 mo

facts.content: Symptoms began about two months ago, coinciding with starting a new, stressful retail head-office job.
facts.source_text: Onset ~2 mo, coinciding w/ new, stressful retail head-office job

facts.content: Patient dreads work and interactions with her boss.
facts.source_text: dreads work/boss interactions

facts.content: Patient experiences daily anxiety, especially in the mornings, with difficulty getting out of bed.
facts.source_text: Daily anxiety esp mornings; difficulty getting out of bed

facts.content: Patient has sleep-onset insomnia, achieving about 3–4 hours of sleep and waking before the alarm with a racing heart and panic.
facts.source_text: Sleep-onset insomnia; ~3–4 h sleep; wakes before alarm w/ racing heart/panic

facts.content: Patient reports palpitations that are perceived as irregular, lasting from minutes to about 10 minutes, and are new in the last two months.
facts.source_text: Palpitations: perceived irregular; lasts minutes to ~10 min; new in last 2 mo

facts.content: Patient denies true chest pain but reports discomfort associated with a fast heart rate.
facts.source_text: no true CP, only discomfort w/ fast HR

facts.content: During the day the patient has low energy, anhedonia, feels on edge, socializes less, and has reduced running and tennis.
facts.source_text: Daytime: low energy, anhedonia, on edge; ↓ socializing; ↓ running/tennis

facts.content: Public transport, particularly the tube, is stressful for the patient, and anxiety is mainly focused on work.
facts.source_text: Public transport (tube) stressful; anxiety mainly work-focused

facts.content: Patient reports no prior similar episodes of these symptoms.
facts.source_text: No prior similar episodes

facts.content: Patient reports low mood but denies suicidal ideation and has good family support.
facts.source_text: Mood/Safety: Low mood; denies SI; good family support

facts.content: Patient is eating regularly with increased chocolate intake and no significant change in overall appetite.
facts.source_text: Appetite: Eating regularly; ↑ chocolate; no sig change

facts.content: The patient has not had prior therapy but is open to one-to-one therapy.
facts.source_text: Prior care: No prior therapy; open to 1:1 therapy

facts.content: Patient's mother has a history of depression.
facts.source_text: FH: Mother w/ h/o depression

facts.content: Patient lives with her parents.
facts.source_text: SH: Lives w/ parents

facts.content: Patient drinks alcohol more heavily on Fridays and Saturdays, sometimes more than recommended, and also drinks occasional wine on weekdays.
facts.source_text: etOH heavier Fri/Sat (sometimes > recommended) + occasional weekday wine

facts.content: Patient is an occasional smoker.
facts.source_text: occasional smoker

facts.content: Patient denies use of other drugs.
facts.source_text: no other drugs

facts.content: Patient works at a fashion retailer head office.
facts.source_text: Occupation: Fashion retailer head office

facts.content: Clinician assesses work-related anxiety with insomnia and functional impact, with no suicidal ideation.
facts.source_text: 1) Work-related anxiety w/ insomnia and functional impact; no SI

facts.content: Clinician assesses palpitations as likely anxiety-related, brief morning episodes that are perceived as irregular without true chest pain.
facts.source_text: 2) Palpitations, likely anxiety-related; brief, morning episodes, perceived irregular, no true CP

facts.content: Patient to self-refer to NHS talking therapies for cognitive behavioural therapy, with a link to be sent.
facts.source_text: Self-refer to NHS talking therapies (CBT); link to be sent

facts.content: Patient advised to start recommended online resources immediately.
facts.source_text: Start recommended online resources now

facts.content: Sleep hygiene advice will be provided in the notes.
facts.source_text: Sleep hygiene advice to be provided in notes

facts.content: Safety-net advice given to call back if symptoms worsen or if unable to cope with work or activities of daily living.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: call back if worsening or unable to cope w/ work/ADLs

facts.content: Consideration of medications if there is inadequate response to therapy and resources, noting they are not first-line.
facts.source_text: Consider meds if inadequate response to therapy/resources (not first-line)

facts.content: Basic blood tests are to be arranged, and the patient is to call to book them.
facts.source_text: Arrange basic blood tests; patient to call to book

facts.content: Patient to have a GP follow-up one week after blood tests to review results.
facts.source_text: GP FU 1 wk post-bloods to review results

facts.content: Clinician observed that the patient appeared quite distressed.
facts.source_text: Affect: Appears quite distressed (per clinician observation)
